topic: Economic and Ecological Importance of Microorganisms
title: Who Makes Curd? Microbes Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Every night, Diya's mother sets curd with one spoon of old curd. Diya wonders who does the work while they sleep. The same tiny workers puff up idli batter and turn a compost pit into soil.

A live zoom ladder goes from a bowl of curd to the clumped milk proteins, the rod-shaped lactic acid bacteria (Lactobacillus) and the lactic acid they make, and milk turns into curd step by step. Then microbes at home (idli and dosa batter, baker's yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae), in medicine and industry (Penicillium, Aspergillus niger), on farms (Rhizobium, Nostoc and Anabaena) and for energy (methanogens and biogas). Economic vs ecological importance side by side, nature's recycling loop with decomposers and diatoms, a worked match of six microbes to their jobs, the exam trap on idli batter, an original NEET match-the-following question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 20 of our PUC Biology series.
Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
